summary: Screw-pile light at the Wicomico River mouth in Maryland, lit 1884. Its wooden house came down in 1966.

structures.note: House on a screw-pile foundation; dismantled in 1966

access.note: Not open to the public. LighthouseFriends notes distant views of the foundation from the shore.

events.note: Lighthouse Board recommended a light at an estimated $15,000

corrections.current: tower, screwpile, wood, built 1884, 11.3 m, standing
corrections.proposed: steel skeletal tower on the old screwpile foundation, built 1966; 1884 wooden house dismantled 1966
corrections.why: The Society's record and LighthouseFriends both say the 1884 house was dismantled in 1966 and replaced by a steel tower on the old foundation. Whether that tower stands today is not settled by the sources read.
The Society's record and LighthouseFriends both give the light 37 feet (11.3 m) above water (mean high water).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1882 recommendation and the 1883 appropriation are the start of the project. The first lighting on 15 August 1884 is confirmed by LighthouseFriends and the Chesapeake timeline, and the Society's record gives 1884 for the house.
The Society's record gives discontinued in 1965. LighthouseFriends and the Chesapeake timeline give deactivation in 1966, when the house was replaced. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Roster: 39 archive lines, matched by name and position (0.76 km); lines copied as printed. Duplicate archive line for Harold M. Messick (1936) merged. William F. and Walter F. McDorman are separate in the archive; the sources read do not say whether they were one man or two. Walter F. McDorman's 1925-1937 and 1937-1948 stints share one person slug. Archive vs LighthouseFriends: Gordy Z. Parks first assistant 1937-1943 (archive) vs 1937-1945 (LF); Leonard H. Staubly 1900-1904 vs 1900-1905. The 6 October 1920 rescue: Bulletin 1920 text says assistant keeper; Bulletin index and Commissioner FY1921 say keeper; the Commissioner report also says Virginia (error for Maryland). The 1918 year for the December rescue comes from LighthouseFriends and the Chesapeake timeline; the Bulletin text gives only '13 December'. The 1905, 1942 and 1943 items come only from the Chesapeake timeline and are not checked against the newspapers it cites. The 1940 ice removal is checked against the Wilmington Morning Star (AP, 27 January 1940). The Lighthouse Board report for fiscal 1884 (construction) is not in the local corpus (lhb covers 1891-1901); construction details come from LighthouseFriends's transcription and are cited to it. The Chesapeake timeline says construction took 32 days; its own dates (17 July to 9 August) do not match that and the story does not use the figure. Present status conflicts: LighthouseFriends says a modern light is exhibited from the old foundation; the Society's record says not existing and not an active aid. Coast Guard present-day status not checked. Record corrections: structure (1884 house gone 1966); focal height (7.6 m in record vs 37 ft / 11.3 m in USLHS and LighthouseFriends). Record position (38.214365, -75.879398, OSM) agrees with LighthouseFriends (38.214372, -75.879402); the USLHS place coordinates are about 0.8 km off and were not used. The light characteristic in the record (Fl W 6s) is not confirmed by any source read here and is not in facts. Daniel A. White: the 1922 obituary (Evening Capital, Annapolis) names Daniel Asbury White as keeper at Shark's Fin and at Great Shoal; the archive's roster lists him as first assistant at both. Linked as other_stations on the 1895-1900 line, cited to the obituary. The same link should go on the Sharkfin Shoal research (1900-1901 line). No women keepers or keepers' families are named in the sources read. The USCG Historian's page (history.uscg.mil) returned 403 live and through the archive, so it was not used. Wikipedia was used only for leads. Not sourced: what hazard the shoal posed, the Maryland General Assembly's 1882 request (Wikipedia only), and the lens's present location. The story says nothing on these. Vernon Cooper (USCG, at least 1951) appears in the roster only, not in the prose. Fact-check 2026-10-28: corrected Powell's role in the 1914 rescue (assistant, not keeper), stated the LighthouseFriends end date for Gordy Z. Parks (1945) against the roster's 1943, noted the Bulletin's 'assistant keeper' for McDorman on 6 October 1920 and the Commissioner entry's Virginia error, and limited the 1905 Baltimore Sun reference to the timeline's source list. Read: Bulletin pages verified by PDF page; 1899 index p. 102 confirmed; Commissioner scan 665 confirmed by text (page image not read).
